summary.title: Tetris tutorial in C++ platform independent focused in game logic for beginners
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a Tetris clone in C++ by storing pieces as 5x5 rotation matrices, using a pivot block for rotation, and checking collisions on a board array, with SDL used only for drawing rectangles.
takeaways: Store each Tetris piece as four 5x5 matrices, one per rotation, so rotating means choosing the next stored matrix instead of doing rotation maths.
Use a 5x5 matrix with a pivot block (value 2) so all rotations stay aligned around the rotation point without translation adjustments.
Keep the board as a 2D array of free or filled cells and check collisions by comparing a piece's matrix against the board and its limits.
Delete completed lines by scanning rows for full blocks and shifting upper rows down.
Game logic is kept separate from drawing, so only the SDL rectangle-drawing layer needs to change when you add graphics.
summary.summary: The tutorial walks through building a Tetris clone in C++ in under an hour, focusing on game logic rather than graphics. Pieces are defined as 5x5 integer matrices for each of four rotations, with 2 marking the pivot block, and a separate table stores initial screen offsets for each piece. A Board class holds the filled/free grid and implements collision checks, piece storage, line deletion and pixel conversion, while a Game class handles random piece creation and drawing via a simple IO layer on SDL rectangles. The page includes the full code snippets for each class and notes the source is Creative Commons licensed, with Windows (Visual C++) and Linux (makefile) builds. The page text is cut off partway through the Game class drawing code.
